# Check of M0-d-05b — re-check on the owner's WSL2 machine (lane `check/M0-d-05b`, re-dispatched 2026-10-04, 22:50 local)

Lane `check/M0-d-05b` (Opus 5.5, Claude Code on the owner's Windows 11 PC inside WSL2 Ubuntu — Linux x64, Intel
i9-10900K, 20 logical CPUs, 16 GiB, Node 24.12.0; flow `flow-7`, stage group 10, J173). The seat is an
implementer-side independent checker and not the item's author. It was re-dispatched after the move to this machine.
The RESUME rule pointed at the closing verdict PASS (lane `check/M0-d-05b-close-r1`, L-0141, below). Before returning
it, the seat re-ran the attribution and the item's local tests. The tests are red on this machine, so this round
replaces that PASS. Ledger row: **L-0149**. No git command was run, and no file of the item was changed. One vitest
process ran at a time, with `--maxWorkers=2`. `free -m` showed 13 747 MB available of 15 950 MB.

## Verdict: FAIL — one blocker (F-5): the harness test times out under this machine's contention

* **Attribution is unchanged.** `corepack pnpm landed:verify -- flow-7 --item M0-d-05b` gave
  `landed:verify flow-7 --item M0-d-05b: ok (1 record)`. The same command gave `ok (1 record)` for
  `check-M0-d-05b` and for `check-M0-d-05b-notes`.
* **The item's tests are red here.** The command was
  `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/model/test/match`. It went red three times out of three, at
  load averages between 17 and 22 on 20 CPUs while other flow seats ran:
  * Run 1: `Test Files  1 failed | 5 passed (6)` · `Tests  1 failed | 45 passed (46)`.
  * Runs 2 and 3: the same test failed. The file alone gave `Tests  1 failed | 6 passed (7)`.
  * Each time, the failing test was
    `synthetic.test.ts > … > runs each set through the harness and reports per-entity time in the record shape
    (CONTENDED; nothing asserted on a time)`. The error read `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.` at 5060 ms, 6069 ms
    and 8286 ms.
  * A builder re-dispatch logged these tests green at 22:50 (`docs/lane-events.log`), before the load rose. So the
    result depends on the machine's load, not on the code.
* **The code's results are right.** The failed runs still printed every record, with the right shape and counts, for
  example `[M0-d-05b contended] metropolis: point 13.712 µs × 80000`. The fault is in the test's time bound, not in
  the routine.

### F-5 (BLOCKER) — a contended wall-clock bound gates the item's test gate

* **Line:** `packages/model/test/match/synthetic.test.ts` line 47, the harness test.
* **What it does:** The test runs `timeMatch` with 3 repeats over all four synthetic sets: district, city,
  city-unrelated and the 80 000-entity metropolis. It runs under vitest's default 5 000 ms test timeout, because
  `plat/vitest.config.ts` sets no `testTimeout` and the test passes none.
* **Why that is a blocker:** A timeout is a timing bar in disguise. M0.md §0.1 (5) says a timing "taken while other
  seats run is **CONTENDED** and never gates" (C-0025, C-0047). This test gates the item's local test gate
  (`--project model`) on how fast the shared machine runs. Under J180, a gate that exits non-zero because of the
  item's files is a blocker. The flow's integration check of stage group 10 runs the whole suite while other seats
  run, so it would hit the same timeout.
* **The neighbouring tests are at risk too.** In the same contended run, "the outcomes: …" (line 32) took 2828 ms, and
  "the classes add up to the whole call on a real set …" (line 145) took 1252 ms. Both are under the same
  5 000 ms default.
* **Required change:**
  1. Give each whole-set test in `synthetic.test.ts` (lines 32, 47 and 145) an explicit generous timeout. 120 000 ms
     follows the kernel's own whole-set tests, for example `rng.test.ts`'s `}, 120_000);`. Alternatively, cut the
     harness test's work, for example 1 repeat on metropolis, and keep the record-shape assertions.
  2. State the reading in the fix round's choices row: no test of the item depends on wall-clock speed, and the
     repeats stay as many as the record shape needs.
  3. Re-run the item's tests on this machine while other seats run, and quote the result.
  4. Make no change to the routine, the harness or any assertion.

This round adds no minor note. N-1 and N-2 in `checks/M0-d-05b-notes.md` stand.

## Verdict: FAIL — four failing lines (F-1 – F-4); every gate is green

The routine is sound on what its tests pin. The sort key is (distance, old id, fresh id). The grid only gathers
candidates and never quantises a match. The brute-force reference, the outcomes, the split tie and the mint
round-trip are all solid. Four findings fail the item:

* **F-1** (line 3, *no undeclared shortcut*: a silently narrowed bar). The timing harness times only part of the
  routine. Between 28 % and 46 % of each `match` call runs outside every kind's probe, and no choices row declares
  this.
* **F-2 – F-4** (line 2, *every test id the item lists is implemented*, and J169's rule that a non-equivalent survivor
  of a targeted mutant needs a test). Three targeted mutants survive. Each breaks a promise the item states. For each,
  a test that the item's code passes and the mutant fails was shown in the mirror.

**The checker's note: the sort key and the grid (CONFIRMED).** `Pairs.assign` sorts by
`s[a] - s[b] || o[a] - o[b] || f[a] - f[b]` over index lists already sorted by id (`byItemId`, UTF-16 code units). The
score is the exact squared distance in integer cm², which orders pairs exactly as the distance does. Every grid's cell
is `radiusCm` per (kind, family). `gridNear` reads the 3 × 3 cells, and a pair is formed only when `d2 <= r2`. The test
"matches by distance, never by quantised cell" passes. K03 (farthest first), K04 (exclusive radius), K05 (accepting the
whole 3 × 3 neighbourhood) and K06 (centre cell only) are all red. K01 and K02 (the old-id and fresh-id ties reordered)
survive and are equivalent. In this seat's own check, greedy assignment under (score, old, fresh) and under
(score, fresh, old) gave `differing assignments 0 of 300000` on random tiered bipartite sets. The author's 200 000 sets
agree.

32 were red: K03–K09, K11, K12, K14–K24, K26–K36. These cover the sort, the inclusive and exact radius, the 3 × 3
neighbourhood, the family on both sides, the bridge's river, a fresh reference not read through succession, the
overlap threshold and family, carry events (always, or one lane only), the split heir order, boundary covering, the
covering tie, survivors kept out of matching, `liveSetOf` retired flags, the dropped hand-on, a tombstone reported as
kept (a silent re-bind), the spine distance, IoU over the union, the `contended` default, refusing references to later
kinds, the family in a key, the per-partition first pass, anchor matching before the split, the `on` and unread-cell
checks, `supersededBy` as a provisional id, duplicate old ids, survivor and provisional-id ambiguity, and overlap
covering. Equivalent: K01 and K02 (above). **Survivors, not equivalent:** K10, K13 and K25 (F-2 – F-4). For each, a
probe test in the mirror (`zz-checker.test.ts`, deleted with the mirror) passed on the item's code
(`Tests 3 passed (3)`) and was red under the mutant (`K10 …: killed`, `K13 …: killed`, `K25 …: killed`).

## Failing lines and required changes

**F-1 (line 3): the timing harness times only part of the routine — a silently narrowed bar.** `timeMatch` sums only
the time between each kind's `probe(kind, 'begin')` and `probe(kind, 'end')`. In `match.ts`, the first probe fires
inside the per-kind loop (line 298), after `checkAnchors`, `prepare` of every old and fresh entity (point checks,
`prepareArea`, `prepareLine`, key checks) and the split checks (lines 221–276). Building the frozen result (lines
596–608) also runs after the last probe. The bar is "≤ 2 µs per re-derived point-anchored and ≤ 20 µs per
overlap-anchored entity, median" for "the routine" (§6.3 *Budget*; §16 M0 (d)). The time outside the probes is not
small. Measured on the built package (`scratchpad/c05b/scope.mjs`, five repeats, medians, CONTENDED and informative
only):

```
district total ms 2.33 probed ms 1.27 share outside probe 0.456
city total ms 112.34 probed ms 72.42 share outside probe 0.355
metropolis total ms 345.71 probed ms 248.61 share outside probe 0.281
```

On the district set, the probed figure (≈ 1.9 µs per entity in the test's print) is under the 2 µs budget, but the
whole call is not. C-0188 (12) says the harness "times each kind through the probe". It does not say that the shared
preparation is left out, and no row gives a reason. **Required change:** time the whole routine. Two ways would do:
prepare each kind's entities inside that kind's probed span, or add a probed preparation phase whose time is shared
across kinds by their entity counts. In either case, every millisecond of a `match` call must count in some kind's or
class's figure. Alternatively, keep the per-kind spans and add the whole call's per-entity time per class as the gated
figure. Declare the choice in a choices row, citing §6.3 *Budget*. Pin it with a fake-clock test that counts clock
reads and checks that the class figures add up to the whole call.

**F-2 (line 2): C-0188 (2)'s "a fresh reference to a fresh entity never equals an old address" has no test.** Mutant
K10 survives. It changes `refFresh` to return `handedOn.get(ref) ?? ref`, so an unmatched fresh entity's provisional id
stands for itself. The case is real: a provisional id is the entity's natural address (C-0188 (1)), so a re-derivation
that re-mints the same key can give a fresh river the old river's address even when the river has moved and is no
successor. Under K10, a fresh bridge on that new river takes the old bridge's address, a succession on the wrong
river. Probe P1 shows it: old `water:a` (0–10 000) with `bridge:o` on it; fresh `water:a` at 50 000 (no successor)
with `bridge:f` at the same point on it. The item gives a tombstone for both, and the mutant fails that. **Required
change:** add this test, and the same case for a key kind (a district whose seed feature is an unmatched fresh entity
carrying the old address).

**F-3 (line 2): the listed test "a way matched by end junctions" pins only the fresh side's end order.** Mutant K13
survives. It drops the sort of the *old* way's end pair, so an old way listed `[b, a]` no longer matches a fresh
`[A, B]`. The test "in either order" reverses only the fresh way's ends, and every old way in `way.test.ts` lists its
ends in sorted order. Probe P2 shows it: old `way:w` with ends `['junction:b', 'junction:a']`. The item gives `succeed`
by key, and the mutant fails that. **Required change:** add a case with the old way's ends in reverse order (and with
both sides reversed).

**F-4 (line 2): the harness's per-class divisor is not pinned on a mixed set.** Mutant K25 survives. It divides the
point class's time by the point *and* overlap entities. The only fake-clock test uses `district`, which has no overlap
entity, so the two divisors agree there. The record's promise is "µs per re-derived old entity" per class (C-0188
(12)), and it is not pinned. Probe P3 shows it: one junction and two water bodies, a clock advancing 0.5 ms per read.
The item gives point 500 µs and overlap 250 µs, and the mutant fails that. **Required change:** add a fake-clock test
on a set with both classes. It goes with F-1's test.

## Notes (not failing)

* N-1: `MatchResult.old`, `addressOf`, `handedOn`, `supersedes` and `perKind` are plain `Map`s. The outcomes inside
  them are frozen, but the maps are not. Harmless at M0, since no caller mutates them.
* N-2: a fresh anchor may name an id that is neither a fresh provisional id nor a survivor, but a *retired* old
  address. That input is malformed, because a producer names fresh ids or survivors. `refFresh` passes such a reference
  through as the old address, and it then compares equal to the old side. The routine could refuse it (PLAUSIBLE; not
  probed further).
